approved: Broadband, Communications and the Digital Economy

Moved the Public Interest Media Advocate Bill 2013, proposing an independent statutory office to decide news media diversity transactions, assess self-regulatory schemes and complaints processes, and operate without ministerial or government direction.

Minister Conroy confirmed no one has been approached for the Public Interest Media Advocate role and that the government will follow Nolan principles and consult on appointments, defending the legislative process by citing two inquiries and extensive public debate.
